outcome: maternal complications (uterine rupture, abnormally invasive placenta, surgical site infections)
cohort: Participants were all women who gave birth at the General Referral Hospital of Walikale, North Kivu, DRC, between January 1 and March 31, 2024.
finding: The caesarean section rate was 15.7%, with the majority (50%) of CS performed in women with a previous caesarean section (Robson group 5), and notable rates of uterine rupture (5.8%) and abnormally invasive placenta (3.7%) among those with a prior CS.
mod_finding: The majority of caesarean sections (50%) were performed in women with a previous caesarean section, while vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) rates were high (71.2% after one and 50.0% after two previous CS), but associated with safety considerations like uterine rupture and abnormally invasive placenta.
